metadata.note: The Louisiana and Arkansas Railway: William Buchanan's Bodcaw Lumber road from Hope, Ark. via Stamps and Minden to Winnfield and Alexandria, La., with the Minden - Shreveport line (1910) and the Jena Branch and Vidalia extension. Controlled from 1928 by Harvey Couch's group, which leased the Louisiana Railway & Navigation Co. (1928/29); Kansas City Southern control from 20 Oct 1939. Per CLAUDE.md Rule 4 every line is split at the end of 1939 into an L&A-coloured feature (company "Louisiana and Arkansas Railway") and, where service is proven after 1939, a Kansas City Southern-coloured feature sharing the same track, with the KCS colour pulled programmatically from kcs-southern-belle in shreveport_railroads.geojson. The L&A colour is new to the dataset.
metadata.researched_from: research/branches/louisiana_and_arkansas_railway.txt (2026-11-12): ICC valuation abstract; winnfield.winnfreenet.com; history-hunts-warehouse (quoting James R. Fair); Fowler Louisiana SL 248 and Arkansas SL 251 station lists; Chronicling America; TSHA; Official Guide Jan 1952.
metadata.ownership_split: 1939/1940 L&A -> Kansas City Southern (control 20 Oct 1939, kcshs.org; Fowler says 1938 - conflict, see not_yet_sourced). The 1902 L&A Railroad -> L&A Railway reorganisation and the 1928 Couch stock purchase are not splits. Split features share track; the L&A pieces (cut at Stamps, Mulberry, Winnfield and Packton because their start years differ) together cover the same line as the joined KCS feature.
omitted: Blocks [8]-[11], the L&A-name years 1930-1939 on the ex-LR&N Shreveport - Coushatta - Alexandria - Simmesport - Torras/Filston, Angola - St. Francisville - Baton Rouge and Baton Rouge - New Orleans line: NOT drawn here. The existing kcs-southern-belle feature in shreveport_railroads.geojson already draws that corridor (in KCS colour, back to 1897) and is not edited in this change; drawing L&A segments on it would double-draw the corridor. See not_yet_sourced for the defects this leaves on that feature.

Block [13] Bodcaw-era Stamps - Spring Hill (1897 Official Guide) and block [14] Belmont - Bussey (1896 Guide): the operating company's name is not established, so they cannot be labelled (Rule 6) or coloured (Rule 4).

Block [15] Taylor Branch, Taylor - Pope - Shady Grove - Cassida - Sydney - Palestine - Newton - Fomby (23.3 mi, 1900 [ANCHOR] in the Official Guide): NOT drawn because its route could not be located. None of the stations geocodes (Nominatim finds only an unrelated Fomby in Little River County, Ark.), there is no tagged grade in OSM or OHM, and the only nearby "Fomby"/"Shady Grove" names are roads in Webster Parish, La. (32.95-32.96 N, 93.17-93.29 W) whose order contradicts Fowler's mileposts. Drawing it would invent geometry; it needs a period map (USGS topo or a county map) first.
Block [16] Tioga Branch (Pineville - Ems) and block [17] ex-LR&N Winnfield Branch (Aloha - Winnfield) in the L&A era: no confirmable passenger year.
Optional 1928 [ANCHOR] on the Vidalia extension (secondary source only): left off, as the report recommends.
Shreveport - Waskom and Greenville - McKinney/Dallas on the LA&T: not part of the 1933 anchor as the report states it.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: kcs-minden-alexandria ends 1951 (last confirmed year, Feb 1952 Guide; Nos. 9/10 ran to 1967/68 on some route); la-jena-branch and la-vidalia-extension end 1921 (last confirmed; service probably ran to the 1945/46 Louisiana Midland sale). [OPEN] starts (earliest proven years, not openings): la-stamps-minden and la-minden-mulberry 1900, la-mulberry-winnfield 1904, la-winnfield-packton 1905. A 1930s-40s L&A timetable and a 1955-65 KCS timetable would settle most of these.

la-packton-alexandria starts 1906, the year the line was placed in operation (Fair; WINN; ICC says 1907); the first passenger timetable in hand is 1909. The research report recommended 1908; 1906 was chosen by the tracing pass.
Shreveporter end: 24 Jan 1962 (Wikipedia L&A, WINN) vs 1961 (chicagorailfan.com); drawn to 1961.
KCS date: control 20 Oct 1939 (kcshs.org), ICC approval May 1939 (Time) vs Fowler "part of Kansas City Southern Lines from 1938". If 1938 is right the colour boundary moves one year.
Jena branch start: first passenger train 1 May 1904 (local history) vs through service Feb 1905 (Fair); drawn from 1905.
Mulberry's position is interpolated by milepost (see geometry_quality); Shreveport Central/Union Station and Alexandria Union Depot sites were not located, so those ends stop in the city centres.
LA&T 1933 anchor: which section the passengers rode, and the company colour/label for an L&A-controlled affiliate (drawn in the L&A colour as a family colour).

EXISTING-LAYER DEFECTS NOT FIXED HERE (shreveport_railroads.geojson, kcs-southern-belle, which this change does not edit): (1) its 1907-1939 and 1897-1907 segments draw Shreveport - Coushatta - Alexandria - Baton Rouge - New Orleans in KCS colour, but 1929-1939 on that track the trains were the Louisiana & Arkansas's (lessee of the LR&N from 1928/29; KCS control only from 20 Oct 1939) and before that the S&RRV/LR&N's - a Rule 4 split is owed (L&A colour 1930 [OPEN]-1939 per report blocks [8]-[11]); (2) its 1939-1940 segment draws the 1940 Huey P. Long bridge alignment, but in 1939 the through trains still used the Torras - Angola car ferry and the east-bank Angola - St. Francisville - Baton Rouge line, and the year was L&A's; (3) whether its 1940-1953 geometry between Moreauville and Lettsworth follows the loop the L&A abandoned in 1953 (history-hunts-warehouse) or the later cut-off is unchecked (Rule 2 later-alignment question). Fix suggestion from the report: split kcs-southern-belle at Shreveport; south of it KCS colour 1940-1969 only, L&A features 1930-1939 on the pre-1940 ferry route, LR&N features for 1899-1923.

segments.note: Hope - Stamps - Spring Hill - Minden - Shreveport, the Shreveporter (Nos. 3/4), inaugurated 30 Dec 1928 with a through St. Louis Pullman via the Missouri Pacific at Hope (Wikipedia L&A; Winnfield history page). Kansas City Southern colour from 1940: Colour/company split at the end of 1939 (CLAUDE.md Rule 4): KCS acquired control of the L&A on 20 Oct 1939 after ICC approval (kcshs.org; Time, May 1939); Fowler says "part of Kansas City Southern Lines from 1938" - a conflict recorded in metadata. From 1940 the L&A lines were timetabled and managed as "Kansas City Southern Lines" (Official Guide), although the L&A stayed a separate KCS-controlled corporation until 1992. Jan 1952 Official Guide table 3 "HOPE, MINDEN AND SHREVEPORT" shows trains 3/4 with recoverable times, air-conditioned and diesel-powered, with a St. Louis - Shreveport sleeper. END CONFLICT: the Shreveporter was discontinued "January 24, 1962" (Wikipedia L&A; Winnfield history page) vs "discontinued in 1961" (chicagorailfan.com); drawn to the earlier 1961 rather than invent a year. No later passenger train Hope - Minden was found. headway_min 1440 = one train each way daily per the 1952 table; earlier KCS years are not counted.

Packton - Pineville was also used jointly by the Rock Island, whose trains are not drawn here. L&A main line south. Nos. 9/10 lasted to 1967/68 (chicagorailfan.com) but whether they kept this routing after 1952 is not established - do not extend without evidence. headway_min 1440 = one train each way (Nos. 9/10) in the 1952 table; 1940s frequency not counted.

segments.note: L&A Jena Branch: Packton - Sardonia - Zion - Georgetown (Missouri Pacific crossing) - Zenoria - Grant - Searcy - Trout - Good Pine - Jena. Built to Jena by 24 Dec 1903 (Winnfield history page; ICC). START CONFLICT: "the first passenger train ... arrived in New Jena on May 1st, 1904" (local history quoted on history-hunts-warehouse) vs Fair: "through service from Packton to Jena could not be provided until February 1905" (Little River bridge unfinished); collapsed to the later 1905. Proven years: 1905, 1909 (Colfax Chronicle advertisement, double daily passenger service "ON JENA BRANCH", Jena 4:45 p.m. / 7:05 a.m.), 1913 (Fowler "Grant 1913t", a company timetable), 1917 and 1921 (the Vidalia - Alexandria trains, which could only run via Jena and Packton; Concordia Sentinel 2 Apr 1921). END IS [OPEN]: 1921 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT an ending - service very likely ran on toward the 1945/46 sale of Packton - Vidalia to the Louisiana Midland, but no source dates it; do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 = the two trains each way of 1909; not sourced for other years.
sources: Segment-level: start 1905 from Fair via history-hunts-warehouse (conflict with 1904 recorded); 1909 from the Colfax Chronicle advertisement (6 Feb 1909 p3, 2 Oct 1909 p3); 1913 from Fowler La. table 17; 1921 [OPEN] from the Concordia Sentinel, 2 Apr 1921 p4 (Chronicling America).

Overpass via maps.mail.ru; opstrace.py for the traced parts.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 46.8 mi against 47.9 mi documented (Fowler La. table 17: Jena 28.9 - Vidalia 76.8). Approximated: 8.1 mi in six straight-line legs between Jonesville and Concordia Junction (Ferriday), where OSM holds only fragments of the abandoned grade - 1.7 mi at Jonesville including the Black River crossing (91.850 W - 91.824 W), 0.2 mi (91.817 - 91.815 W), 1.6 mi west of Wildsville (91.798 - 91.772 W), 0.4 mi (91.760 - 91.755 W), 3.4 mi (91.694 - 91.637 W) and 0.6 mi (91.625 - 91.616 W); each chord joins two mapped pieces of the same east-west grade, so the drawn line stays within a few hundred metres of the true alignment. 38.7 mi on OSM ways: Jena - Jonesville on old_railway_operator=KCS, Concordia Jn - Vidalia on old_railway_operator=MP (abandoned). Mileposts from Jena: Jonesville 23.4 traced vs 22.8, Wildsville 25.8 vs 24.9, Concordia Jn 39.0 vs 39.2. Wildsville - Concordia Jn was the ex-Natchez & Western (3 ft gauge, later standard-gauged by the Iron Mountain); the line is drawn on the grade as last mapped, not checked against the 1917 alignment.

segments.note: L&A Vidalia extension: Jena - Rhinehart - Archie - Jonesville - Wildsville Junction, then Missouri Pacific (ex-Iron Mountain / New Orleans & Northwestern) track leased or rented by the L&A through Frogmore and Concordia (Ferriday) to Vidalia, opposite Natchez. Jena - Wildsville Jn was built by the L&A in 1913 (ICC) but has no passenger evidence before the through service, so 1913-1916 are not drawn. START: daily Vidalia - Alexandria service inaugurated 1917 - Donaldsonville Chief, 18 Nov 1916: the L&A "has bought the tracks of the Iron Mountain road extending from Vidalia to Jonesville La and on Jan 1 will inaugurate a daily train service between Vidalia and Alexandria" vs Winnfield history page "Service began July 1, 1917" - the date conflicts, the year agrees. END IS [OPEN]: 1921 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT an ending - Concordia Sentinel, 2 Apr 1921 p4, prints a letter from the L&A Passenger Traffic Manager about discontinuing only an extra Jonesville run, so the regular trains continued. A secondary statement that passengers could still book from Concordia Junction in 1928 (history-hunts-warehouse, no primary cited) is NOT drawn. Service very likely ran on toward the 1945/46 sale to the Louisiana Midland; do not extend without evidence. headway_min 1440 = the "daily train service" of the 1916 announcement.
sources: Segment-level: start 1917 from the Donaldsonville Chief, 18 Nov 1916 p2 and the Winnfield history page (date conflict recorded); 1921 [OPEN] from the Concordia Sentinel, 2 Apr 1921 p4 (Chronicling America); track ownership from the ICC valuation.

properties.line: Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas: Waskom – Greenville
properties.speed_source: estimate: no running times found; ~40 km/h assumed for a thin mixed-type service. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap old_railway_operator=KCS ways Jefferson - Greenville (today CPKC) and OpenHistoricalMap "Sherman Shreveport and Southern Railway" ways Waskom - Jefferson (the ex-MKT line the LR&N of Texas took over in 1923), traced with opstrace.py.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 147.9 mi Waskom - Jefferson - Hughes Springs - Daingerfield - Pittsburg - Winnsboro - Sulphur Springs - Greenville. Documented: TSHA gives 181 mi McKinney - Louisiana state line for the whole LA&T, and this piece omits McKinney - Greenville (roughly 30 mi), so about 150 mi is expected - a loose check only, as no station mileposts were in hand. 116.1 mi on OSM (old_railway_operator=KCS, Jefferson - Greenville), 31.8 mi on OpenHistoricalMap (Waskom - Jefferson, 27.1 mi, on the lifted SS&S grade, plus short OHM pieces elsewhere); no straight-line legs. All waypoints within 0.5 km. Not drawn: Shreveport - Waskom (the former T&P route that Fowler says became the LA&T) and Greenville - McKinney/Dallas, because the report's anchor names only Waskom - Greenville. Which part of the line the 1933 passengers rode is not stated by the source.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] 1933 is the single proven passenger year for the Louisiana, Arkansas & Texas (the LR&N of Texas, renamed 14 Apr 1930, L&A-controlled, merged into the L&A 1 Jul 1939): TSHA - in 1933 "Earnings that year were $3,567 from passengers" and the road owned "eleven passenger cars". Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed: no passenger year is proven for 1923-1932 under the LR&N of Texas name here or for 1934-1939, and nothing after 1939 in L&A or KCS colour (by Jan 1951 the Official Guide index daggers Hughes Springs, Pittsburg, Farmersville and Lorraine as freight only; table 5 "Shreveport and Dallas" has no recoverable times). Do not widen this anchor without evidence. $3,567 a year is a few passengers a day - probably a mixed train; headway_min is a guess of one train each way daily, unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1933 from the TSHA Handbook entry for the Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas Railway. Route section, headway and train type not sourced.

properties.colour_note: Drawn in the Louisiana and Arkansas colour as a family colour: the LA&T was controlled by the L&A from 1930 and merged into it in 1939 (TSHA). A judgement recommended by the research report (UNRESOLVED 5), not a claim that they were one company.
